contents.Header2: Adding album art to a folder

contents.Text: You can add album art to an entire folder with a file or a directory, named after one of these types. They are used if no embedded image is found in a file, and they are checked in this order, where the first match is used:
[[[warning:Note:]]] The names are not case sensitive, so [[[strong:Cover]]] and [[[strong:cover]]] both work.

rows: Name it after the type, with a supported extension (e.g. album_art.png)
Any images inside with a supported format are randomised and used as album art

contents.Text: [[[warning:Note:]]] For each name, the directory is checked before the file.
If you want to override any embedded images or the normal album art, use one of these types instead:
[[[warning:Note:]]] The [[[strong:override]]] types take priority over all other album art, including embedded images. They are checked in the order shown, and work the same way as the normal types.
If no embedded image and none of the names above are found, the folder the song is in is checked for any image, whatever it is called.
If there is [[[strong:exactly one]]] image in the folder, it is used as the album art, as it is probably the cover.
If there are two or more images, nothing is used.
[[[warning:Note:]]] This only applies to the normal types, not the override types.
